## [verb (1)](https://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/verb)

re·​lease[ri-ˈlēs](https://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/release?pronunciation&lang=en_us&dir=r&file=releas01 "How to pronounce release (audio)")

released; releasing

[Synonyms of _release_](https://www.merriam-webster.com/thesaurus/release)

Take our 3 question quiz on release

Simple Definition A Simple Definition is available from our Learner's Dictionary to help you understand the meaning faster. 

[transitive verb](https://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/transitive)

1

**:**to set free from restraint, confinement, or servitude

release hostages

release pent-up emotions

release the brakes

also**:**to let go **:**[dismiss](https://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/dismiss)

_released_ from her job

Take our 3 question quiz on release

2

**:**to relieve from something that confines, burdens, or oppresses

was _released_ from her promise

3

**:**to give up in favor of another **:**[relinquish](https://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/relinquish)

release a claim to property

4

**:**to give permission for publication, performance, exhibition, or sale of

also**:**to make available to the public 

the commission _released_ its findings 

release a new movie

[intransitive verb](https://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/intransitive)

**:**to move from one's normal position (as in football or basketball) in order to assume another position or to perform a second assignment

 Choose the Right Synonym for _release_

[free](https://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/free), [release](https://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/release), [liberate](https://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/liberate), [emancipate](https://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/emancipate), [manumit](https://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/manumit) mean to set loose from restraint or constraint.

[free](https://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/free) implies a usually permanent removal from whatever binds, confines, entangles, or oppresses.

_freed_ the animals from their cages

[release](https://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/release) suggests a setting loose from confinement, restraint, or a state of pressure or tension, often without implication of permanent liberation.

_released_ his anger on a punching bag

[liberate](https://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/liberate) stresses particularly the resulting state of liberty.

_liberated_ their country from the tyrant

[emancipate](https://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/emancipate) implies the liberation of a person from subjection or domination.

 labor-saving devices _emancipated_ us from household drudgery 

[manumit](https://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/manumit) implies emancipation from slavery.

 the document _manumitted_ the enslaved men

## Word History

Etymology

Verb (1)

Middle English _relesen_, from Anglo-French _relesser_, from Latin _relaxare_ to relax

Noun

Middle English _reles_, from Anglo-French, from _relesser_

First Known Use

Verb (1)

14th century, in the meaning defined at [transitive sense 1](https://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/release#h1)

Noun

14th century, in the meaning defined at [sense 1](https://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/release#h2)

Verb (2)

1828, in the meaning defined [above](https://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/release#h3)

## Legal Definition

release

1 of 2 transitive verb

re·​lease

released; releasing

1

a

**:**to relieve or free from obligation, liability, or responsibility

the debtor is _released_ from all dischargeable debts

b

**:**to give up (a claim, title, or right) to the benefit of another person **:**[surrender](https://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/surrender#legalDictionary)

2

**:**to set free from confinement

was _released_ on personal recognizance

release

2 of 2 noun

1

a

**:**discharge from an obligation or responsibility that bars a cause of action

did not effect a release of the school for any negligence

b

**:**the giving up or renunciation of a right or claim that bars a cause of action

was a release of the remainder of the debt

Note: A release may in some situations require consideration in order to be valid. A release of one joint obligor sometimes is considered to release all the obligors.

2

**:**an act or instrument that effects a release

signed a release issued by the insurer

called also release of all claims

 compare [hold harmless](https://www.merriam-webster.com/legal/hold%20harmless)

3

**:**the act or instance of freeing especially from custody
